digest.component_or_area: Gerrit Verified CI/CD pipeline and test execution
propositions: Ubuntu default/integration pytest jobs occupy 1,812 runner-seconds (30.2 minutes) per Verified run due to redundant YAML parsing in bridge cadence, repeated Pandoc subprocesses in corpus/hardening tests, and test fixture setup overhead; these are distributed mechanisms, not a single long pole.

The bridge cadence test reads and parses the same workflow YAML 1,440 times, consuming 7.653 seconds of the 130.59–100.66s per-test duration; hoisting the parse to session scope eliminates this redundant I/O while preserving the exhaustive minute-by-minute invariant proof.

Pandoc hardening tests invoke 3,421 subprocesses (884 units × current + legacy pair) when the legacy assertions are proven invariant across all 884 units; replacing legacy subprocess execution with immutable committed expected outputs reduces contention while keeping all 884 live product conversions on real Pandoc.

Gerrit Verified jobs with superseded patchsets remain queued indefinitely when job-level always() predicates prevent GitHub cancellation, causing 20–25 minute stale-run admission delays; replacing always() with !cancelled() status checks preserves full fallback while enabling prompt replacement admission.

The live Jira DC integration suite (tests/external/live_jira_dc) is already routed outside Gerrit Verified by the 'not external' selector and runs in a dedicated weekly/manual external-integration workflow with 2,384–2,635s occupancy, so moving it saves zero per-change runner occupancy and is not a viable optimization lever.

Post-remediation successful full-route runs (31900214367=25m53s, 31903956917=22m47s, and prior clean samples) demonstrate that distributed reductions across bridge cadence I/O, static Pandoc oracle, AST provenance indexing, complexity singleton routing, and build-provenance fixtures preserve all test coverage while bringing end-to-end Verified latency into the 20–30 minute target band, with no individual pytest phase exceeding 30 seconds.
